pr_title: kvserver: use engine only after entry cache
pr_body:
Raft entries are often in the entries cache. This PR decouples `term` and `entries` fetching to prepare for the refactoring, and moves constructing a storage Reader strictly after checking the cache, to reduce the overhead.

Fixes #92274
Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/92326)
@tbg This is now ready for a full review.

issue_context.title: kv: pebbleReadOnly constructed in replicaRaftStorage.Entries even when reading from entry cache
issue_context.body:
I noticed in a recent round of benchmarking that we construct a `pebbleReadOnly` in `replicaRaftStorage.Entries` even in the vastly common case where all entries are served out of the raft entry cache:

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2a041d61d021f563828597fe9961f54727419c1d/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_raftstorage.go#L102

This is wasteful.

I would have made the fix of pushing this into `entries` myself, but there's was just enough friction due to `term`'s [use of the `reader`](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2a041d61d021f563828597fe9961f54727419c1d/pkg/kv/kvserver/replica_raftstorage.go#L296) that I figured I'd leave it to the experts.

Is it worth asking whether this code needs to operate on a LSM snapshot? There should not be concurrent mutation to the state it is looking at.

Jira issue: CRDB-21690

Epic CRDB-220
comments: @tbg @pavelkalinnikov This seems like something we could easily address as part of the ongoing Raft log storage work.

Worth noting that this construction doesn't look particularly heavy:
https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/2ace40eba5e9a9423231d7a73dfa6db0c0128263/pkg/storage/pebble.go#L1887-L1903

But in principle, it makes sense to reverse the order.

Yeah, good point -- this isn't taking out an engine snapshot immediately, it's pinning the iterators on first access, reusing existing pooled iterators. This is probably cheaper than constructing a new iterator straight from the engine when we do end up using it though.

@nvanbenschoten Since you bring this up, I assume construction of `pebbleReadOnly` showed up prominently enough in these benchmarks to make it worth optimizing, even though the construction cost is just fetching a pooled struct and reinitializing it?

It wasn't prominent in these benchmarks, but it did jump out when looking at a CPU profile of kv0 and focusing on Raft. The pebbleReadOnly construction accounted for about **0.1%** of the total CPU profile. However, Raft itself was only about **10%**, so you can back into this being around a **1%** savings in the compute work performed by Raft. Here's the one screenshot I captured of this (a week or so ago). That's not a huge saving, but it is still probably worth doing while we're working in this area. I think there's also something nice about not touching the engine until we need to.

review_comments: Probably also need to return a "bad" error if index > ts.Index (and < lastIndex). This would mean that there is a gap.
